domain.name: Unreal Engine Production
domain.description: Program-specific Unreal Engine operation covering editor workflow, Actors and Components, Levels and World Partition, Blueprints, C++, materials, Niagara, animation, Control Rig, Sequencer, lighting, profiling, and packaging. Version-sensitive feature details should be checked against current documentation when needed.

competencies.name: Unreal Editor, Content & Project Structure
competencies.description: Navigate Unreal Editor panels, Content Browser organization, project settings, plugins, assets, and source-control-friendly project layout.
competencies.purpose: Keep Unreal projects understandable and prevent content, reference, and configuration drift as they grow.

units.title: Unreal assets are referenced objects, not loose files
units.content: Maps, Blueprints, materials, textures, meshes, animations, data assets, and other packages reference each other. Renames and moves should be performed with reference awareness and redirector cleanup rather than treated like arbitrary filesystem changes.

units.title: Project organization workflow
units.content: Define folder and naming rules; separate project-owned content from third-party packs; review enabled plugins; establish maps, Blueprints, art, audio, UI, data, and developer areas; use editor-aware moves; save and validate references after restructuring.

units.title: Project-structure failures
units.content: Avoid mixing marketplace or plugin content directly into core project folders, leaving redirectors unresolved indefinitely, enabling plugins without need, and renaming heavily referenced assets outside the editor without validation.

drills.title: Organize a production Unreal project
drills.prompt: An Unreal project has imported marketplace content, custom Blueprints, test maps, duplicated materials, and unclear ownership. Design a cleanup plan that preserves references.

competencies.name: Actors, Components, Levels & World Structure
competencies.description: Build runtime objects using Actors and Components and organize worlds using Levels, streaming, and large-world structures.
competencies.purpose: Create reusable gameplay and environment structures without fragile level-specific duplication.

units.title: Actors are containers for composed runtime behavior
units.content: Actor Components, Scene Components, Child Actor patterns, data assets, and inheritance each solve different reuse problems. Composition usually scales better than deep inheritance when responsibilities are independent.

units.title: World-structure workflow
units.content: Define world boundaries and persistent systems; decide what belongs in reusable Actors versus level-only placement; use components for independent capabilities; establish streaming or partition strategy for large worlds; test loading, unloading, and actor ownership under play.

units.title: World-structure failures
units.content: Avoid giant monolithic Actors, duplicating logic per level, relying on hidden level references inside reusable actors, and building large environments before deciding streaming and ownership conventions.

drills.title: Structure a reusable city block
drills.prompt: Plan Unreal Actor/component and level organization for a city block containing modular buildings, traffic props, lights, interactables, and streamed surroundings.

competencies.name: Blueprint Visual Scripting
competencies.description: Build maintainable Unreal gameplay and tool logic using Blueprint classes, functions, events, interfaces, dispatchers, and data-driven patterns.
competencies.purpose: Use Blueprints as structured software rather than an unreadable collection of connected nodes.

units.title: Blueprint design workflow
units.content: Define responsibility and state; choose Actor, Component, Function Library, Interface, Data Asset, or other suitable type; use functions and macros intentionally; prefer events over constant polling where possible; name variables and execution paths clearly; test construction and runtime behavior separately.

units.title: Readable Blueprint graphs are part of correctness
units.content: Small functions, clear execution flow, reroute nodes, comments, typed interfaces, and bounded responsibilities make visual scripts easier to debug and safer to change than giant Event Graphs.

units.title: Blueprint failures
units.content: Avoid heavy logic on Tick by default, casting chains across unrelated systems, hard-coded level actor references in reusable classes, duplicated graphs instead of reusable functions/components, and hidden state changes inside sprawling execution paths.

drills.title: Build a reusable Blueprint interaction framework
drills.prompt: Design a Blueprint system supporting doors, seats, pickups, and prompts without hard-coding each class into the player Blueprint.

competencies.name: Unreal C++ & Blueprint Integration
competencies.description: Use Unreal C++ classes, reflection macros, modules, components, and Blueprint exposure in a maintainable hybrid architecture.
competencies.purpose: Place performance-sensitive or reusable systems in code while preserving designer-friendly Blueprint control where useful.

units.title: Unreal C++ participates in an engine reflection system
units.content: UObjects, Actors, Components, properties, functions, garbage collection, modules, and Blueprint exposure follow engine-specific ownership and reflection rules beyond ordinary C++ semantics.

units.title: Hybrid code workflow
units.content: Define system responsibility; choose UObject, Actor, Component, subsystem, or plain struct/class appropriately; expose only necessary properties and functions to Blueprint; respect object ownership and lifecycle; compile incrementally; test editor hot-reload-sensitive changes with clean restarts when needed.

units.title: C++ integration failures
units.content: Avoid storing unmanaged pointers to engine objects without ownership awareness, exposing every internal detail to Blueprint, putting designer-tunable data only in code, and assuming C++ constructor or editor-time behavior matches runtime initialization order.

drills.title: Design a reusable C++ component with Blueprint controls
drills.prompt: Plan an Unreal component implemented in C++ for core behavior but configurable and event-visible in Blueprint.

competencies.name: Materials, Shaders & Niagara
competencies.description: Create reusable Unreal materials and Niagara effects while controlling visual complexity and runtime cost.
competencies.purpose: Build scalable visual systems that remain art-directable and performant.

units.title: Material and VFX graphs are runtime programs
units.content: Texture samples, branches, translucency, particle counts, overdraw, dynamic parameters, and simulation stages all carry costs. Visual graphs should be treated as executable systems, not free decoration.

units.title: Material and effect workflow
units.content: Define surface or effect behavior; build a reusable master/material-function structure where appropriate; expose instance parameters; keep texture channel conventions consistent; prototype Niagara emitters with bounded spawn and lifetime; test overdraw and shader complexity in representative scenes.

units.title: Material/VFX failures
units.content: Avoid unique one-off materials for every prop, unnecessary translucency, particle systems with unbounded spawn, using expensive effects to hide lighting problems, and assuming editor preview cost equals scene cost.

drills.title: Build a material plus lightweight effect
drills.prompt: Plan a reusable weathered-neon sign material and a subtle Niagara flicker/spark effect for repeated urban props.

competencies.name: Animation, Control Rig & Sequencer
competencies.description: Work with skeletal animation, Animation Blueprints, Control Rig, root motion, retargeting, and Sequencer for runtime and cinematic motion.
competencies.purpose: Create motion systems and cinematics that remain editable and integrate cleanly with gameplay.

units.title: Animation integration workflow
units.content: Validate skeleton and scale; import clips with known frame/root conventions; configure retargeting where needed; separate locomotion state from additive/upper-body layers; use Control Rig for procedural or editor-time adjustment; use Sequencer tracks with explicit ownership of transforms and animation.

units.title: Only one system should own a transform at a time
units.content: Gameplay movement, root motion, Sequencer, Control Rig, physics, and Blueprint transforms can fight each other. Define authority per state and transition ownership explicitly.

units.title: Animation/cinematic failures
units.content: Avoid duplicate transform ownership, retargeting without checking pose/base skeleton assumptions, foot sliding from mismatched root policy, and Sequencer overrides that leave gameplay actors in unexpected state after playback.

drills.title: Build a gameplay-to-cinematic interaction
drills.prompt: Plan an Unreal sequence where the player triggers a short door-entry cinematic and then returns cleanly to gameplay control.

competencies.name: World Building, Lighting & Rendering
competencies.description: Assemble large environments using modular assets, landscape/world systems, lighting, reflection, exposure, fog, and render features.
competencies.purpose: Create readable, performant worlds with coherent visual hierarchy and scalable content organization.

units.title: Environment build workflow
units.content: Establish world units and coordinate policy; block traversal and sightlines; place modular kits before bespoke detail; define streaming/partition cells; set exposure and broad lighting; validate reflections, shadows, atmosphere, and navigation; add hero detail after performance and scale are stable.

units.title: Large-world quality depends on hierarchy and streaming
units.content: A believable world does not require every object to be unique. Modular repetition, HLODs/LODs, instancing, culling, partitioning, and selective hero detail create scale without overwhelming memory and render budgets.

units.title: World-building failures
units.content: Avoid placing final detail before scale and traversal are validated, unbounded shadow-casting lights, inconsistent exposure between zones, hero-density detail everywhere, and discovering streaming problems only after the full map is assembled.

drills.title: Plan a real-world neighborhood build
drills.prompt: Design an Unreal workflow for recreating a real neighborhood from GIS/reference data using modular buildings, hero landmarks, streamed surroundings, and nighttime lighting.

competencies.name: Unreal Profiling, Optimization & Packaging
competencies.description: Measure game-thread, render-thread, GPU, memory, streaming, shader, and asset costs and prepare stable packaged builds.
competencies.purpose: Deliver projects that work outside the editor on target hardware instead of relying on editor-only success.

units.title: Performance and packaging loop
units.content: Define target hardware and frame/memory budgets; test standalone or packaged builds; capture timing and GPU evidence in representative scenes; identify dominant bottleneck; make one meaningful change; compare before/after; verify maps, cooked assets, plugins, configuration, and package output.

units.title: Optimize measured bottlenecks
units.content: Geometry, shadows, materials, Niagara, Blueprint Tick, physics, streaming, and memory stress different systems. Use engine profiling tools to identify the limiting path instead of applying generic reductions everywhere.

units.title: Optimization/package failures
units.content: Avoid judging performance only in editor viewport, lowering global quality before locating hotspots, packaging without testing clean-machine assumptions, and changing many systems at once so cause and effect become unclear.

drills.title: Diagnose a long-street performance drop
drills.prompt: An Unreal city scene drops below frame target only when looking down a long street. Build a profiling plan covering visibility, geometry, materials, shadows, lights, and streaming.
